newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary wheat prices rise as Serbia seen buying.
newsitem.headline: Hungary wheat prices rise as Serbia seen buying.

text.p: Budapest Commodity Exchange milling wheat futures rose on Monday following a modest firming of world prices and continued talk in Hungary of potential sales to Serbia, traders said.
Almost all wheat futures rose the 400 forints per tonne limit. May wheat finished up 400 forints at 23,860 and December closed at 21,900, up 400.

"World market prices rose and prices here followed them," said Janos Szojka of Swap Ugynoki Kft. "Also there has been buying pressure since the middle of last week following a long period of price falls."
Other dealers added wheat prices had been also boosted by unconfirmed market talk of rising Serb demand for Hungarian wheat.
"Export opportunities are said to have arisen in Serbia," Termin Broker's Robert Vajo said. "There may be demand, but there are serious concerns about its financial coverage."

Hungary has over 500,000 tonnes of the 1996 crop for which traders have not seen buyers so far and some dealers were still pessimistic, saying that foreign markets easily accessible to Hungary were already saturated.
"Earlier (in 1996) the prices were too high (for competitive exports), and now it is too late," Szojka said.

However, wheat was expected to rise further in the next few days on further market talk of Serb demand and also as correction of the past few months' slump amounting to thousands of forints, traders said.
